subject: Starlumen migration inquiry — stepwise retention incentives & onboarding economics
messages:
From: Jill Park <jill.park@starlumen.ai>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@starlumen.ai
Date: 2028-03-22T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Evaluating vendor switch — pricing details attached

Connor —

Thanks for taking this. We are running a short list evaluation to replace our current inference vendor (contract attached) and would like a straight economics comparison from Redwood. High level: we’re at ~9M tokens/month (steady-state), peak concurrency ~35 requests/s (p95 latency target 180ms), and we have 120-seat internal developer access. Data residency: US only; SOC2 in place.

Procurement is asking for two things from any vendor: (1) a written price-match or equivalently attractive onboarding credit that keeps our 12-month TCO neutral vs current pricing, and (2) a clear breakdown of any hidden onboarding costs (services, egress, account seat mapping). We’d also like a 90-day pilot option with a migration SLA and an opt-out rollback path.

I attached our current contract and a quick procurement sheet. Can you get me a proposal (numbers + short migration checklist) by EOD Friday?

Attached: Current_Contract_Starlumen_2027.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Jill Park
Head of Platform, Starlumen.ai
jill.park@starlumen.ai
From: connor.obrien@redwood.ai
To: Jill Park <jill.park@starlumen.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-22T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluating vendor switch — pricing details attached

Hi Jill —

Appreciate the context and the contract. Quick clarifying Qs before we put numbers together:
- Is the 9M tokens/month evenly distributed or seasonal spikes beyond the stated peak?
- Any strict latency SLA below the 180ms p95 you mentioned for critical routes?
- Are all 120 seats full-access inference users or a mix of dev/test seats we can treat differently for billing?
- Do you have any on-prem / dedicated-only workloads or is this all acceptable in our hosted regions?

We typically approach these with three commercial levers depending on risk appetite:
1) A matched-compute-rate + onboarding credit (one-shot credit to offset migration costs)
2) Tiered retention incentive — deeper discounts tied to committed volume + seat bundles and an initial canary pilot with credits for the first 90 days
3) Hybrid (dedicated for sensitive workloads + hosted for the rest) for customers who need EV/SE parity.

If you’re open, I’d propose a short 30-minute call today or tomorrow to align on the migration checklist and which lever you prefer — that will help us tailor the exact credit structure. I’ve attached our internal econ checklist so you can see items we consider.

Attachments: redwood_econ_checklist.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks —
Connor O'Brien
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai
From: Jill Park <jill.park@starlumen.ai>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@starlumen.ai
Date: 2028-03-22T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluating vendor switch — pricing details attached

Connor —

Responses inline:
- 9M tokens is our steady-state; we see monthly spikes up to ~13–14M during model retraining windows.
- Latency: 180ms p95 is our maximum tolerable; for production endpoints we prefer <120ms but can accept 180ms for some back-office routes.
- Seats: ~80 full-access developer seats, 40 view-only / test seats — we can tier those in a bundle.
- No on-prem workloads; US regions only.

Procurement reiterated the ask: if Redwood can provide a written match (or better) on compute unit economics for the first 6–12 months plus a migration/onboarding credit that materially reduces our migration burn, we’ll prioritize Redwood in the short list.

Requested deliverable: a short written proposal with 2–3 commercial options (numbers + migration checklist + expected go-live timeline) so procurement can circulate internally. We’re available for a 30-min sync tomorrow morning PST.

Attached: starlumen_procurement_sheet.csv (csv)

Thanks —
Jill
From: connor.obrien@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-22T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Evaluating vendor switch — proposal ask from Starlumen (see below)

Karthik / Mina —
Forwarding Starlumen’s ask. Key points: 9M steady-state (spikes to 14M), 80 full seats + 40 view/test, latency tolerance up to 180ms p95 (preferred <120ms for production). They want a written price-match or onboarding credit to keep 12-month TCO neutral + migration checklist and a 90-day pilot.

Quick Econ run (very rough):
- Current vendor compute effective rate (from their sheet): $0.00045 / token equivalent.
- Our standard hosted rate for comparable workload: $0.00055 / token.
- Delta: ~22% higher list price vs their current.

Suggested proposal (3 options to present to Starlumen):
Option A — Conservative match
- 25% discount on list for year 1 (bringing us closer to their price)
- $50k onboarding credit (professional services + runbook)
- 60-day pilot with no charge up to 5M tokens

Option B — Aggressive match (preferred by AE)
- 40% temporary match on compute unit price for first 6 months (effective price ~ $0.00033/token)
- $30k onboarding credit + 2 engineer-days of onboarding support included
- 90-day pilot (up to 10M tokens)

Option C — Pilot-first minimal commitment
- 3-month free pilot up to 10M tokens, then standard list pricing with a 20% discount for first 3 months after pilot

Risks / asks:
- Any credit >$30k needs leadership approval / finance sign-off.
- If we do Option B (40% match), ops must confirm we can meet the <120ms p95 for their critical endpoints on our hosted infrastructure; otherwise we should propose hybrid dedicated for sensitive routes.

I’ve pasted Jill’s original thread below for context. Can you weigh in with recommended option, delta on the numbers, and whether we can commit to the 90-day pilot SLA? Also note: procurement wants a written doc by EOD Friday — pushing timeline.

—Connor

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: connor.obrien@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-22T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Evaluating vendor switch — proposal ask from Starlumen (see below)

Connor / Mina —

Thanks for the clear summary. My take: we should push Option B with the following edits to keep legal / finance exposure reasonable:
- Adjust the temporary match to 35% (versus 40%) for the first 6 months — still compelling and reduces runway cost.
- Approve a $30k onboarding credit (within AE delegation). Anything >$30k routed to deals desk / CRO approval.
- Commit to the 90-day pilot SLA but add an explicit rollback clause: if we don’t meet <180ms p95 for critical endpoints within 30 days post-migration, Starlumen may revert to their prior provider for those endpoints and we offer a prorated credit.
- Include a 60-day early-payment discount (1.5%) to improve cash flow.

Ops to validate the <120ms p95 on hosted regions for critical endpoints before we promise it in writing — if we can’t guarantee, propose dedicated for those routes and quantify delta.

If that sounds ok, AE can send the written proposal with the three options and Karthik-approved numbers. We’ll flag the $30k credit and 35% match in the offer and include the rollback SLA and early-pay discount.

—Karthik
